#### Practice Exercise

Reading about addition helps, but practice is essential for real understanding. Below is an addition written vertically, column by column, from the units to the hundreds.

The values are checked as you type. If a digit is wrong, the squares are colored to match the number you wrote, and a tip reminds you of the complement. If the sum carries, the squares beyond the group of ten are colored, showing the digit that stays in the column. When both values are right, the squares fill in, a congratulation appears, and the button that moves to the next column is shown.

Before typing, look at the complement of the value already in the column: the complement tells you how many squares are still missing to reach ten. If the bottom digit is at least the complement, the sum reaches ten and 1 is carried to the next order; the squares left outside the group of ten are the digit that stays in the column.

When you finish the calculation, you can move on to the next problem by clicking the button below.

#### Practicing Addition with Typed Values

In each column, add the bottom digit of the second number to the value already in the column. Type the digit that stays in the column in the result row, and, if the sum reaches ten, type 1 in the carry box above the next order. Before typing, look at the complement of the value already in the column: if the bottom digit is at least the complement, the sum reaches ten and 1 is carried to the next order; the squares left outside the group of ten are the digit that stays in the column.
